title: What Technical Due Diligence Finds When the Deck Says “70% Automated” — Soukaïna Abelhad
talk_summary: A due-diligence talk arguing that AI automation claims must be checked by arithmetic (workload vs. fully loaded human labor), precise definitions (AI-attributed vs. straight-through processing), and validated evaluation (automated graders are more optimistic than expert reviewers). It ends with a unit-economics formula: cost per accepted autonomous task, including review, escalation, and rework.

takeaways.technique: Validate the automated judge against expert ground truth
takeaways.what_they_do: They compare automated grader decisions to blinded expert maintainer decisions on the same patches, and measure the gap and what bad output escaped.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Meta found 24% point gap between automated grader and merge decision after adjustment to the human baseline.
takeaways.numbers: 24 percentage-point gap; 296 AI-generated PRs; 4 maintainers from 3 repos

takeaways.technique: Track review burden as AI output volume grows
takeaways.what_they_do: They pair workload volume with fully loaded human labor (reviewers, operators, rework) to detect whether AI is assisting or actually removing labor.
takeaways.numbers: 98% more PRs merged; +91% review time; +154% PR size; 10,000+ developers, 1,255 teams

takeaways.technique: Straight-through processing rate per named workflow
takeaways.what_they_do: They define automation on a ladder (AI drafted / human edited / human approved / no human intervention) and measure the straight-through rate inside an explicitly named boundary.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Define it as a complete end-to-end without human intervention inside a boundary you name.

takeaways.what_they_do: They compute unit economics as eligible workflow value × adoption × STP success × accepted quality, minus AI cost, human review, escalation, and rework.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The metric I would want is cost for accepted autonomous task. If the task fails, escalates, or need rework, this belongs to the cost.

takeaways.technique: Turn warnings into gates, not reports
takeaways.what_they_do: They cite Builder.ai where a public warning existed but the process never converted it into a blocking gate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the warning existed, but the process did not turn it into a gate.

takeaways.what_they_do: They require evaluation to report escaped defects, not just pass rates, and to name who labeled ground truth and whether experts agree.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Ask what the automated judge was validated against, and ask what bad output escaped.
takeaways.numbers: 10/10 output passed automated validation; 'barely few survive' expert review
